summary: Family-scope propagation, contradiction-summary tombstones, and screened-filer clearance rules: added a compact canon surface fixing propagation of family-wide findings into linked public lineage and dashboard objects, visible tombstone withdrawal rather than deletion for public anonymous contradiction summaries, and expiry / reinstatement logic for screened or quarantined filing status, then threaded it through the research stack and synchronized release metadata to the new current revision.
why_this_counts: The archive had already fixed review authority, research threshold, protocol transparency, incident notice, minimal incident objects, privacy tiers, comparison discipline, visible restatement, instability thresholds, public remediation states, stale-warning escalation, bounded contest, phased reactivation, shielded contradiction, evidence floors, and slice-versus-family correction and serial-escalation rules.

But those gains still left three quiet failures: family-wide findings could remain visible only in one privileged record, unsafe or fundamentally misleading contradiction summaries could disappear instead of leaving historical trace, and screened filing status could either drift indefinitely or quietly self-clear.

The new doctrine adapts conservative official ingredients already visible in current governance: per-trial notification despite shared breach, stable identifier and versioning practice, preserved public version history rather than deletion, and formal expiry-or-reinstatement logic for screened or suspended participation.

The revision stays narrow. It does not yet fully specify the exact lag clock and public mismatch semantics for stale linked records, the minimum successor-link semantics for withdrawn contradiction tombstones, or the review rule for repeated use of protected bypass routes during screened status.
The next gap is therefore narrower again: lag markers, tombstone successor semantics, and protected-bypass review.
status_change: advanced the research-governance layer from scope-exact, correctable, and serial-capture-resistant superseding-notice governance to propagation-complete, publicly non-disappearing, and screened-clearance-disciplined superseding-notice governance
